pin_history.what_happened: The live manifest moved to e46eefd3... during the run. Both tools refused it, and this lane stopped and did not re-pin on its own authority.
pin_history.authority: Orchestrator pin notice: use close/1cor_landed_outputs_manifest.frozen_for_close_lanes.v1.json, sha256 e46eefd38aa481b2618b49de6b193acac12be8a8d418cc40223dbf342d560c4c. That single pin change supersedes the brief's value; every other pin stands. REPORTED by the orchestrator.
pin_history.tested: work/patch2.py: the frozen file has the notified digest; it lists 112 outputs; the digest of every output but review/D3_result.json appears in the pre-patch record (MEASURED). No earlier manifest copy exists, so its non-output fields were not compared. Class counts other than closing_message did not change (MEASURED).

changes_after_the_notice: patch2: the authorised pin and path change. It also added review/D3_result.json to not_opened_rules as a closing message. The notice did not name this step, but an unclassified output stops the generator by design. The file was not opened; it is named by the manifest's digest only.

The tools had been patched before the stop and never built, and the record on disk was stale, so the record was regenerated. This went beyond the notice's minimum because the cursor required it. Nothing was restarted.

patch3, parameters only, not the pin: audit found the word 'strategy' in quoted text, 170 times in the audit's count. It now renders as the reading plan and is on the blocklist, guarded for 'rhetorical strategy' and 'argumentative strategy'. The body now holds 0 (MEASURED by audit3).

changed_and_why: Every book-specific name, path, digest and count moved to book_params.v1.json (TE-7); a sub-check tests the scripts for book tokens.

Disagreements are defined mechanically because no reconciling or paired later reading exists in this book's landed files.

limits: 26 outputs listed by the landing receipts have no durable file; they are named with their listed digest only.
6 completion rows carry no digest.
Each gate review had a single reader.
First readings were made after the second revision round and did not read the final text.
No review of the fourth revision round; no logs for rounds 4 and 5.
One reading lens ran on 3 of 10 groups.
Every reader was one model family, and author and grader share weights (grader_models.v3 fallback_in_force true, EXTRACTED). Agreement among them is one voice (OW-19).
No report by a human scholar is among the listed files.
27 open questions are owed to a final review not held and not authorised (OW-30); the record gives them as open.
The WEB licence term is not stated in the book's own files; the record supplies none.
Tool files, drafted entries, candidate plans and revised-entry row files are named with digests and not quoted. 11 closing messages were not opened.
Carried items in the reading plan are quoted only as bytes_show.
Reconciling and rereading shapes are not carried; an unknown class is a hard stop.
Regex literals remain inside some quoted evidence.
Generator and checker share six functions, listed in the check record, so the checker is not independent of them.
Severity ranking is a mapping of the readers' words, not a judgement.
The blocklist is measured, not proven complete: it passed twice while audit still found residue. It has 35 patterns now, one dead. Two blind lanes should not rely on it.
Plain words byte, candidate, flag, field, script, model and digest remain in quotations (MEASURED by audit1 and audit2), and capitalised reader words such as FRAME and RULE remain.

Opaque renderings such as 'a working file' and 'a numbered rule' lose which file or rule was meant, so quoted reasoning can be harder to follow. Some read awkwardly, e.g. 'reading plan a numbered rule'.
9 of 537 Greek script runs in quotations are not exact substrings of the witness files (MEASURED, informational, not a gate, not investigated).
Disagreement is a mechanical definition: a difference of verdict among the readings of one passage, or two or more challenges proposing different courses.
Spot-reading covered section 2, the first dispute entry and targeted searches, not the whole record.

They are the manifest's only landing of the first readings; I took 'open packets by its paths' to authorise this. The orchestrator should confirm, because the same files fall within the words 'all final-message files'.
Two oversized command outputs were persisted to session tool-result files by the harness. They were never opened.

One Grep used a guessed path for the brief (path-not-found) and one Read mistyped an OUT path (not found). Neither returned content and neither was a listing, but the first was not a path the brief names.
A blocked version of build_notes.json and D1_result.json was written during the stop and is replaced by this one; it was never returned.
